nodes.name: Synthesis of NiMoN on Ni foam

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH with iR compensation using CI method
nodes.source_text: For HER, we synthesized two efficient non-noble metal catalysts of MoNi4 and NiMoN supported on Ni foam, as well as commercial Pt/C loaded on Ni foam as a benchmark electrode for comparison. From the polarization curves shown in Fig. 1a, we can observe that both the NiMoN and MoNi4 catalysts show excellent HER activity with iR compensation. Based on the overpotential summary in Table 1, the overpotentials with iR compensation are very small for the NiMoN and MoNi4 catalysts. Even under large current densities of 500 and 1,000 mA cm−2, the overpotentials for NiMoN are only 125 and 167 mV, respectively. However, without iR compensation, the overpotential required by each of the three electrodes increases significantly, especially under large current densities. For the NiMoN catalyst, the overpotential at a small current density of 50 mA cm−2 increases from 43 mV (with iR compensation) to 61 mV (without iR compensation).

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH with iR compensation using CI method
nodes.source_text: For the MoNi4 catalyst, the overpotentials even increase to 427 and 789 mV at the two respective large current densities. Interestingly, the HER activity of NiMoN is slightly worse than that of MoNi4 with iR compensation, but without it, NiMoN is superior to MoNi4. This reversal demonstrates that the NiMoN catalyst has a smaller overall resistance.

nodes.source_text: To provide a possible comparison, we manually determined 80%, 85%, 90%, and 100% iR compensation for HER with MoNi4 and OER with NiFe LDH by an EIS method.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH with manual iR compensation using EIS method at 85% compensation
nodes.source_text: To provide a possible comparison, we manually determined 80%, 85%, 90%, and 100% iR compensation for HER with MoNi4 and OER with NiFe LDH by an EIS method. As shown in Fig. 3c and d, it is clear that the increasing percentage of iR compensation results in a gradual decrease in the HER and OER overpotentials, respectively, at different current densities. To present valid iR compensation and to avoid excessive correction, 85% iR compensation is recommended.

nodes.characterization_summary: HER polarization curves show NiMoN and MoNi4 catalysts exhibit excellent HER activity with iR compensation, superior to Pt/C benchmark. With iR compensation, overpotentials for NiMoN are 43 mV and 59 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 125 mV and 167 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻². Without iR compensation, overpotentials increase to 61 mV and 101 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 376 mV and 713 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the polarization curves shown in Fig. 1a, we can observe that both the NiMoN and MoNi4 catalysts show excellent HER activity with iR compensation, and both are superior to Pt/C.

nodes.characterization_summary: HER polarization curves for MoNi4 catalyst show overpotentials with iR compensation of 41 mV and 52 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 103 mV and 157 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻². Without iR compensation, overpotentials increase to 65 mV and 113 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 427 mV and 789 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: For MoNi4, the overpotentials even increase to 427 and 789 mV at the two respective large current densities.

nodes.characterization_summary: HER polarization curves for Pt/C benchmark catalyst show overpotentials with iR compensation of 52 mV and 96 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 252 mV and 353 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻². Without iR compensation, overpotentials increase to 60 mV and 112 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 461 mV and 880 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: In comparison, the required overpotentials at the same current densities for the Pt/C benchmark are 252 and 353 mV respectively, with iR compensation.

nodes.characterization_summary: OER polarization curves show NiFe LDH and NiFeN catalysts exhibit better OER performance than IrO2 benchmark both with and without iR compensation. NiFe LDH shows overpotentials with iR compensation of 276 mV and 293 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 347 mV and 379 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻². Without iR compensation, overpotentials increase to 296 mV and 341 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 628 mV and 965 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe LDH and NiFeN catalysts exhibit better OER performance than that of IrO2 both with and without iR compensation.

nodes.characterization_summary: OER polarization curves for NiFeN catalyst show overpotentials with iR compensation of 329 mV and 348 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 417 mV and 442 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻². Without iR compensation, overpotentials increase to 343 mV and 389 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 596 mV and 850 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe LDH and NiFeN catalysts exhibit better OER performance than that of IrO2 both with and without iR compensation.

nodes.characterization_summary: OER polarization curves for IrO2 benchmark catalyst show overpotentials with iR compensation of 379 mV and 426 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 542 mV and 592 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻². Without iR compensation, overpotentials increase to 395 mV and 478 mV at 50 and 100 mA cm⁻², and 862 mV and 1182 mV at 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe LDH and NiFeN catalysts exhibit better OER performance than that of IrO2 both with and without iR compensation.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots obtained for HER and OER catalysts and fitted to a simplified Randles circuit to determine series resistance (Rs) values for manual iR compensation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Another method that can be used to conduct iR compensation is manually calculating the series resistance (Rs) from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) Nyquist plots. To obtain the Nyquist plots shown in Fig. S3, we fit the data to a simplified Randles circuit, as shown in Fig. S4, and then used the calculated Rs values to determine 100% iR compensation manually.

nodes.characterization_summary: Overall water-splitting polarization curves for NiFeN||NiMoN electrolyzer show voltages with iR compensation of 1.58 V, 1.61 V, 1.75 V, and 1.83 V at current densities of 50, 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻², respectively. Without iR compensation, voltages increase to 1.62 V, 1.71 V, and 2.30 V at 50, 100, and 500 mA cm⁻², respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFeN||NiMoN electrolyzer exhibits very good activity for overall water splitting with iR compensation. The required voltages are only 1.58, 1.61, 1.75, and 1.83 V at current densities of 50, 100, 500, and 1,000 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HER polarization curves for MoS2 catalyst show similar trends to NiMoN and MoNi4, with large differences between overpotentials with and without iR compensation at large current densities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Very similar results were also demonstrated for a typical transition metal chalcogenide catalyst, MoS2 (Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: OER polarization curves for NiFeP catalyst show similar trends to NiFe LDH and NiFeN, with large differences between overpotentials with and without iR compensation at large current densities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This was further confirmed by analyzing a typical transition metal phosphide catalyst, NiFeP, as shown in Fig. S2.
